topic: Your personality may be a byproduct of your brain's metabolic efficiency
subject: brain

facts.claim: The metabolic cost of song production in the canary, which has the temporally most complex song, was no greater than in the other two species studied.
facts.quote: Surprisingly, the metabolic cost of song production in the species with the temporally most complex song, the canary, was no greater than in the other two species.

facts.claim: Taking steps of equal length did not minimize metabolic cost or mechanical cost when walking on a split-belt treadmill.
facts.quote: We found that taking steps of equal length did not minimize metabolic cost or mechanical cost.

facts.claim: Symmetry was identified as the optimal strategy when energetic cost was estimated from a composite metric that combined both metabolic and mechanical costs.
facts.quote: However, symmetry was identified as the optimal strategy when energetic cost was estimated from a composite metric that combined both metabolic and mechanical costs.

facts.claim: The metabolic cost of singing is similar to that of calling in frogs and of human speech production.
facts.quote: Our analysis shows that the metabolic cost of singing is also similar to that of calling in frogs and of human speech production.

rejected.claim: The average GCoW in YA was 3. 4 ± 0. 4 J/kg/m and 3. 8 ± 0. 4 J/kg/m in OA (~12% more in OA), and the average NCoW in YA was 2. 4 ± 0. 4 J/kg/m and 2. 8 ± 0. 5 J/kg/m in OA (~17% more in OA).
rejected.quote: From all studies reviewed, the average GCoW in YA was 3. 4 ± 0. 4 J/kg/m and 3. 8 ± 0. 4 J/kg/m in OA (~12% more in OA), and the average NCoW in YA was 2. 4 ± 0. 4 J/kg/m and 2. 8 ± 0. 5 J/kg/m in OA (~17% more in OA).

research.angle: While some behaviors like symmetry appear to optimize a composite of metabolic and mechanical costs, complex behaviors like birdsong do not necessarily require higher metabolic costs than simpler ones.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that while some physical movements optimize for energy, complex communicative behaviors do not always show a corresponding increase in metabolic cost.
research.caveat: The sources do not provide direct evidence linking these metabolic costs to specific personality traits.
